body: President Donald Trump visited the construction site of the new White House ballroom on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, signing the final steel beam before a crane lifted it into place on the roof. The visit was his first public appearance since the November 3 midterm elections, in which Democrats made sweeping gains.

The ballroom is being built on the site of the East Wing, which was constructed in 1902 and demolished beginning in October 2025. Trump has described the project as one of the largest and most beautiful ballrooms in the world, with 50-foot ceilings, marble floors and Corinthian columns. The White House has put the cost at about $400 million, funded by the president and private donors, though other published estimates have been higher.

The project has faced legal challenges. The National Trust for Historic Preservation sued in December 2025, arguing that the demolition and construction were unlawful without legally required reviews. In August 2026, the Supreme Court stayed a lower-court injunction, allowing construction to continue while the case proceeds.

Critics, including preservation groups, have objected to the demolition of the historic East Wing and the scale of the new structure. The White House has said the project is tied to the security of the president and the White House grounds, and that the ballroom will serve presidents for generations to come.
imageCredit: The White House, Washington, D.C. — Photo: Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 3.0)
imageNote: Free-licence photo of the White House. No free photo of the ballroom construction itself was available.
summary: President Donald Trump visited the construction site of the new East Wing ballroom on November 4, signing the final steel beam before it was lifted into place.
title: Trump Showcases White House Ballroom as Final Steel Beam Is Raised

body: The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, Nintendo's remake of the 1998 Nintendo 64 classic, launched on November 5, 2026, exclusively for Nintendo Switch 2. The game is listed at $59.99 in the United States.

The remake rebuilds the original's visuals with what Nintendo describes as a puppet-show look, and adds an orchestral soundtrack, fully voiced cutscenes, expanded dialogue and a dedicated jump button — a control the 1998 version never had. It was developed in-house by Nintendo's Entertainment Planning & Development Production Group No. 3, with Monolith Soft contributing to parts of the game design, programming and graphics.

Series producer Eiji Aonuma has said the remake was partly a teaching project: rebuilding the game would help the current, younger Zelda team understand the structure and ideas that made the original special, and carry those lessons into future games. The project also coincides with the 40th anniversary of The Legend of Zelda series.

Early reception has been strong. As of its launch week, the game held a Metacritic score of 96, making it one of the best-reviewed games of 2026. Nintendo says the guiding idea was simple: the visuals may change, but the experience should not.
imageCredit: An ocarina instrument — Photo: Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)
imageNote: No free image of the game itself exists (game artwork is copyrighted). This is a photo of a real ocarina — the instrument the game is named after.
summary: Nintendo's remake of the 1998 classic The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time arrived on Switch 2 on November 5, rebuilt with new visuals, voice acting and modern controls.
title: Ocarina of Time Remake Launches on Nintendo Switch 2 to Strong Reviews
Microsoft 365 Outage Stretches Into Second Day as Fix Attempts Fall Short
summary: Outlook, Teams and Copilot stayed down into Friday after a global Microsoft 365 outage that began on Thursday, with Microsoft saying its fixes were not taking as expected.
imageCredit: Building 92 at Microsoft headquarters in Redmond — Photo: Coolcaesar, Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)
imageNote: Photo of Microsoft headquarters in Redmond.
body: A global Microsoft 365 outage that began on Thursday, November 12, 2026, stretched into Friday, leaving Outlook, Teams, Copilot and other Microsoft 365 apps disrupted for users in 74 countries.

Downdetector, which tracks outage reports, recorded about 130,000 to 140,000 Outlook problem reports at the peak in the United States on Thursday, with reports also coming in from India, Australia, Taiwan and other countries.

Microsoft said a number of its servers became unexpectedly unavailable, putting elevated load on the remaining infrastructure. The company said it was not aware of any malicious activity behind the incident, and there was no indication it was caused by a cyberattack.

On Friday morning, Microsoft reported early signs of stabilisation, but said the changes it had applied were not taking as expected and capacity had not returned to normal. The company has not given a timeline for full restoration.

title: Avril Lavigne Welcomes First Child, a Baby Girl, in Surprise Announcement
summary: The 42-year-old singer shared the news on Instagram on Friday, revealing she had welcomed her first child — a daughter — without ever announcing a pregnancy.
body: Avril Lavigne surprised fans on Friday, November 13, 2026, announcing on Instagram that she has welcomed her first child, a baby girl. The 42-year-old singer had not previously disclosed that she was expecting a child.

She shared three black-and-white photos: a close-up of the newborn's tiny hand held by Lavigne and her partner, Lavigne cradling the baby to her chest, and — a nod to her "Sk8er Boi" days — a skateboard with two adult-size checkered Vans beside a tiny pair of baby Vans. She captioned the post "Our mini [expletive] princess has arrived." She did not share her daughter's name or date of birth, and she has not publicly identified her partner.

The eight-time Grammy-nominated singer-songwriter, known for hits including "Complicated" and "Sk8er Boi", has been largely out of the spotlight in recent months. A representative told ABC News she has been enjoying time with her family while working on a new album, and thanked fans for their love.
The surprise announcement drew a wave of congratulations from fans across social media, many of them noting that the singer had kept both the pregnancy and her partner entirely out of the public eye.
imageCredit: Avril Lavigne performing at Glastonbury Festival, June 2024 — Photo: Raph_PH, Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0)
imageNote: Free-licence photo of Lavigne performing at Glastonbury in June 2024. No free photo of the baby announcement itself exists (her Instagram photos are copyrighted).

title: FAA Lifts Nationwide Ground Stop After Four Hours as Outdated Air Traffic System Fails
summary: The FAA grounded all departing flights across the United States on Friday after an air traffic control communications failure, stranding thousands of travellers for more than four hours before lifting the stop.
imageCredit: Departure board at Chicago O'Hare airport — Photo: Redolta, Wikimedia Commons (CC0)
imageNote: Free-licence photo of a departure board at Chicago O'Hare. The ground stop affected airports across the United States.
body: The Federal Aviation Administration ordered a nationwide ground stop on Friday, November 13, 2026, halting all departing flights across the United States after instability in its radar and communications systems. The order, issued in the afternoon, cited extraordinary circumstances and safety concerns. It was lifted at about 8:15 p.m. ET, more than four hours after it began.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said the failure came from the country's ageing air traffic control system. The FAA began seeing instability in radar and communications at traffic control centres from about 3:36 p.m. ET, as switches and routers in the old analogue system became overloaded with data. Duffy said the system gave inconsistent data from the routers, and the FAA shut it down. Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there was no indication of a nefarious attack, calling it a telecommunication outage.

Nearly 7,000 flights were delayed or cancelled, according to Reuters. More than 3,500 aircraft were in the air when the stop was issued; by 8 p.m., fewer than 400 remained airborne. Flights already in the air were allowed to continue, and exceptions were made for medical, law-enforcement and life-saving cargo flights. US-bound departures from Eurocontrol's 42 member countries were also suspended at the FAA's request.

The disruption was only the third nationwide ground stop in US history, after September 11, 2001, and a computer outage on January 11, 2023. Duffy renewed President Donald Trump's request for Congress to approve $30 billion to upgrade the air traffic control system, saying it would take some time for flights to return to normal, with aircraft and crews out of position.

title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang Resigns After 33 Years Amid Affair and Spy Probe
summary: Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang resigned on November 12, ending his 33-year tenure at the AI chipmaker, after allegations of extramarital affairs and an investigation into whether he was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation.
imageCredit: Jensen Huang speaking at Stanford University, April 30, 2026 — Photo: Anders Eidesvik, Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 4.0)
imageNote: Free-licence photo of Huang speaking at Stanford University in April 2026. No free photo of the resignation announcement itself exists.
body: Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang has resigned from the company he co-founded, ending a 33-year tenure at the helm of the world's most valuable chipmaker. Nvidia announced on Thursday, November 12, 2026, that Huang had stepped down as president, chief executive and board member, effective immediately. Chief financial officer Colette Kress will serve as interim chief executive while the board searches for a permanent successor.

The resignation follows days of mounting scrutiny over Huang's personal life. On November 8, Huang acknowledged he had been unfaithful to his wife and apologised to his family and colleagues, while Nvidia's board opened an independent investigation into whether he had been the target of a foreign intelligence operation. The New York Times reported on November 11 that Huang had also had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of healthcare. Nvidia did not give a reason for his departure.

The controversy centres on Huang's relationship with a Singapore-based tech executive, Alice Huang, whom US intelligence officials suspect of spying for China. US authorities have scrutinised Megaspeed, a Singapore company that buys chips from Nvidia, and concluded it was a Chinese intelligence asset. The board said at the time it opened its investigation that it had no reason to believe US national security interests or Nvidia secrets had been compromised.

Investors reacted sharply: Nvidia's stock plunged by more than 13% after the news broke on November 12, and the roughly $4 trillion chipmaker has shed about $600 billion in market value this week. Huang, 63, co-founded Nvidia in 1993 and built it from a maker of graphics chips for games into the dominant supplier of processors used to train and run artificial intelligence systems. President Donald Trump has suggested former Apple chief executive Tim Cook as Huang's replacement.

title: Two Planes Collide on Miami Airport Taxiway a Day After Nationwide Ground Stop
summary: A Copa Airlines Boeing 737 clipped the nose of a UPS cargo plane while both were taxiing at Miami International Airport on Saturday night, leaving two people with minor injuries.
imageCredit: A Copa Airlines Boeing 737 taxiing after arriving from Panama City — Photo: Adam Moreira, Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)
imageNote: Free-licence photo of a Copa Airlines Boeing 737 taxiing. It shows the same aircraft type and airline involved, photographed at JFK Airport, not the Miami incident itself.
body: Two planes collided on the ground at Miami International Airport on Saturday night, November 14, 2026, just a day after a nationwide flight grounding brought US air travel to a halt. The wingtip of a Copa Airlines Boeing 737 struck the nose of a UPS Boeing 767 while both aircraft were taxiing, the Federal Aviation Administration said. Two people were injured in the collision, which happened at around 9:15 p.m. local time.

The Copa flight had just landed in Miami from Panama City, Panama, carrying 166 passengers and six crew members, and was taxiing towards its gate. The UPS freighter, flight 358, was preparing to depart for Bogota, Colombia. Air traffic controllers had told the UPS crew to give way to the Copa flight, the FAA said, and the two aircraft made contact at the intersection of two taxiways.

Air traffic control audio captured the moments after the impact. “Somebody hit us,” the Copa pilot said. Asked by the controller whether the UPS plane had made contact, the UPS pilot replied: “Yeah, we went too far, and then he clipped us with the wing.” The Copa pilot later reported: “It seems that we are missing the left wingtip.” A photo of the UPS plane showed its nose crumpled, with a gaping hole in the panels.

The two injured people were treated at the scene by fire and rescue teams and did not need to go to hospital, airport communications director Greg Chin told CNN. All 166 passengers and six crew members disembarked and the plane was returned to the terminal. The FAA has opened an investigation, and has not established any connection between the collision and Friday’s nationwide ground stop, which was caused by an air traffic control communications failure. Both airlines said they would cooperate with the investigation.

title: SpaceX Catches Starship Midair in Historic First as Rocket Returns From Orbit
summary: SpaceX caught the upper stage of its Starship rocket with the giant mechanical arms of its launch tower on Saturday, the first time a spacecraft returning from orbit has been plucked out of the air at its launch site.
imageCredit: Starship on its launch pad at Starbase, Texas, before its fifth test flight in October 2024 — Photo: Steve Jurvetson, Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0)
imageNote: Free-licence photo of the full Starship stack on its launch pad at Starbase. No free-licence photo of the November 14 catch itself exists yet.
body: SpaceX caught the upper stage of its Starship rocket midair on Saturday, November 14, 2026, as it returned to its launch site in Texas after a day in orbit — the first time a spacecraft has been caught by a launch tower after flying back from space. The vehicle, Ship 42, emerged from a cloudy sky over Starbase and descended slowly before slipping smoothly between the two giant mechanical “chopstick” arms above Launch Pad 2.

The catch capped a 22-hour mission, the 15th test flight of the world’s largest and most powerful rocket. Ship 42 lifted off on Friday evening, November 13, completed 14 orbits of Earth at about 265 kilometres (165 miles) up, and released 26 advanced Starlink satellites before firing its engines to come home. SpaceX said everything on the spacecraft, including its vital heat shield, appeared to work well.

The mission was only a partial success. The first-stage Super Heavy booster, which was also meant to be caught by the tower arms, ran into trouble shortly after Friday’s liftoff. Its engines stopped firing too soon on the way back down, and its guidance system sensed it was not in the right position, automatically diverting it toward the Gulf of Mexico, where it exploded before hitting the water. SpaceX had already caught returning boosters three times before, and engineers are still investigating the cause.

The achievement was welcomed by NASA, which is paying billions of dollars for Starship to land Artemis astronauts on the Moon later this decade. “It was almost magic,” NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman wrote on X. SpaceX founder Elon Musk congratulated his “incredible team”, and company spokesman Dan Huot said: “We caught a Starship and now, everything changes.” SpaceX expects to begin launching Starships from Florida’s Kennedy Space Center within the next few months.

title: Robert Pattinson Cast as the Next James Bond in Amazon MGM's Bond 26
summary: Amazon MGM Studios announced on Monday that Robert Pattinson, 40, will succeed Daniel Craig as James Bond in the next 007 film, directed by Denis Villeneuve.
imageCredit: Robert Pattinson at the 75th Berlin International Film Festival, February 2025 — Photo: Harald Krichel, Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)
imageNote: Free-licence photo of Pattinson at Berlinale 2025. No free photo of the Bond announcement itself exists (the studio's first-look image is copyrighted).
body: Amazon MGM Studios announced on Monday, November 16, 2026, that Robert Pattinson will be the next James Bond, succeeding Daniel Craig in the role. The studio unveiled the casting on Instagram with a video showing Pattinson emerging as Bond as the classic 007 theme plays. The 40-year-old actor will make his debut as 007 in an upcoming, untitled Bond film from Dune director Denis Villeneuve. No release date has been set.

Pattinson becomes the seventh actor to play Bond in the official film series, following Sean Connery, George Lazenby, Roger Moore, Timothy Dalton, Pierce Brosnan and Craig, whose 15-year tenure ended with No Time to Die in 2021. The new film will be the series' 26th entry, and the first produced since Amazon MGM Studios took creative control of the franchise in 2025. The script is by Steven Knight, with Amy Pascal and David Heyman producing and Tanya Lapointe executive producing.

The casting ends one of the most closely watched searches in Hollywood. In recent weeks, several actors — including Callum Turner, Jack Lowden, Josh O'Connor and Nicholas Hoult — were reported to have screen-tested for the part, according to The Hollywood Reporter. Pattinson has an existing working relationship with Villeneuve, having appeared in the director's forthcoming Dune: Part Three. Puck News reported that Pattinson is signed on for three Bond films.

Pattinson first became a global star as Edward Cullen in the Twilight films and has since built a career as one of Hollywood's most in-demand leading men, including starring as Batman in The Batman and working with Christopher Nolan on Tenet and The Odyssey. The announcement drew an immediate wave of reaction from fans online, many of whom had spent years debating who should take over the role.

title: Peltola Holds 11,000-Vote Lead as Alaska's Last Uncalled Senate Race Nears a Decision
summary: Democrat Mary Peltola leads Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan by more than 11,000 votes in Alaska's still-uncalled Senate race, sitting just short of the majority that would avoid a ranked-choice count on Wednesday.
imageCredit: Mary Peltola's official congressional portrait, 2022 — Photo: Leah Herman, House Creative Services (public domain)
imageNote: Free-licence official portrait of Peltola from her time in the US House of Representatives. No free photo of the Senate race count itself exists.
body: Democrat Mary Peltola has moved to the brink of winning Alaska's closely watched US Senate race, leading Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan by more than 11,000 votes with about 97 per cent of ballots counted. Peltola holds 140,637 first-choice votes, or 49.9 per cent, to Sullivan's 129,424, or 46 per cent, according to the Alaska Division of Elections' unofficial count. The Associated Press has not called the race, which is the last uncalled Senate contest in the country.

Peltola declared victory on Saturday, November 14, after the latest batch of ballots widened her lead. She sits just short of the 50 per cent of first-choice votes needed to win outright. If she finishes below that mark, Alaska will conduct a ranked-choice tabulation on Wednesday, November 18, eliminating the lowest-placed candidates and redistributing their voters' next preferences until one candidate passes 50 per cent. A preliminary ranked-choice tally by FairVote, using the state's ballot records, puts Peltola ahead 51.8 per cent to 48.2 per cent. The state is targeting November 25 to certify the result.

Sullivan's campaign said on Monday that it will not acknowledge the outcome until certification, saying Alaskans deserve a complete and accurate count and that the campaign will let the process run its course until every legal vote is counted and certified. The statement, which put the words "and certified" in bold, signals the incumbent is prepared to wait out the final count. President Donald Trump, who has backed Sullivan, called the race a "disgrace" on Monday.

The count has been shadowed by a federal legal fight. The Justice Department sued before the election to block certification if Sullivan lost, arguing that votes for a retired teacher also named Dan Sullivan — who appeared on the ballot as Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. — could have been cast for the senator by mistake. A federal judge dismissed the case on November 1, saying such an inquiry would breach ballot secrecy, and the department is appealing. Alaska voters also rejected a ballot measure to repeal ranked-choice voting, with 53.5 per cent voting against repeal — the second time they have kept the system since adopting it in 2020.

title: Ukraine Strike Collapses Crimean Bridge Road Span Into the Kerch Strait
summary: A Ukrainian strike overnight collapsed a road arch and span of the Crimean Bridge into the Kerch Strait, cutting the 19-kilometre crossing days before Vladimir Putin is due to meet Donald Trump and Xi Jinping.
imageCredit: The Crimean Bridge in 2019 — Photo: Rosavtodor, Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 4.0)
imageNote: Free-licence photo of the bridge in 2019, before this week's strikes. No free-licence photo of the collapsed span itself exists yet.
body: A section of the Crimean Bridge collapsed into the Kerch Strait overnight on November 16–17, 2026, after a Ukrainian strike, Ukraine's General Staff said on Tuesday. One of the metal arches and the road span beneath it were completely destroyed, the Security Service of Ukraine (SBU) said, and the railway section was also damaged. It was the second strike on the bridge in as many days.

The SBU said the strike was the seventh and final stage of a multi-stage operation carried out over several weeks, in which Ukrainian forces first degraded the air defences, radars and electronic warfare systems guarding the crossing. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the attack was carried out exclusively with Ukrainian-made weapons: Palianytsia missile-drones struck the road section, while Neptune missiles, Ruta drones and FP-5 drones struck the railway section. The SBU said it was its fourth strike on the bridge.

The 19-kilometre (12-mile) road-and-rail bridge, built at a cost of $3.7 billion after Russia annexed Crimea in 2014, is the peninsula's main supply route from mainland Russia and one of President Vladimir Putin's signature projects. Russia's transport ministry said traffic across the crossing was suspended while specialists assessed the damage, and the Kremlin said the bridge would be restored. Russian officials said there were no casualties on the bridge itself, according to preliminary information. Ukrainian defence company Fire Point said more than 270 metres of roadway had been destroyed.

The strike comes days before Putin is due to meet US President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Asia, lending the attack added symbolism. The bridge, the longest crossing in Europe, was built to handle 40,000 cars a day and move 14 million passengers and 13 million tonnes of cargo a year, according to Russian state media. Ukraine has stepped up attacks on Crimea in the past six months, forcing the Russian-installed authorities to impose a state of emergency over the summer because of widespread power outages and fuel shortages on the heavily militarised peninsula.

title: GTA 6 Leads The Game Awards 2026 Nominations With Eight, Two Days Before Launch
summary: Grand Theft Auto VI leads The Game Awards 2026 nominations with eight, including Game of the Year, even though it does not launch until November 19. Six games are up for the top prize, and public voting is now open ahead of the December 10 ceremony.
imageCredit: Geoff Keighley, host of The Game Awards — Photo: Official GDC, Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0)
imageNote: Free-licence photo of The Game Awards host Geoff Keighley. No free-licence image of the 2026 nominees themselves exists.
body: Grand Theft Auto VI leads the nominations for The Game Awards 2026 with eight, including Game of the Year, even though the game does not launch until Thursday, November 19. Host Geoff Keighley revealed the full shortlist across 30 categories in a livestream on Tuesday, November 17, two days before Rockstar Games' sequel reaches players.

Six games are competing for Game of the Year: 007 First Light, Control Resonant, Grand Theft Auto VI, Phantom Blade Zero, Resident Evil Requiem and The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time. Control Resonant and Resident Evil Requiem follow with six nominations each, Phantom Blade Zero has five, and Nintendo is the most-nominated publisher overall with 12. Grand Theft Auto VI is also up for Best Game Direction, Best Narrative, Best Art Direction, Best Score and Music, Best Audio Design and Best Action/Adventure, with Manni L. Perez nominated for Best Performance.

The nominations drew attention because Grand Theft Auto VI was eligible despite not yet being on sale. Games qualified if they were commercially available by November 20 at 9 p.m. Pacific time, and the game's release on November 19 falls inside that window by a single day. Its preloads went live last week, and millions of players are expected to stream launch day later this week.

Public voting is now open on The Game Awards website and runs until December 9 at 6 p.m. Pacific time. Fan votes count for 10 percent of the result in most categories, with a jury of more than 160 media and creator outlets deciding the remaining 90 percent. The winners will be announced at the ceremony on Thursday, December 10, at 4:30 p.m. Pacific time at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles, streaming live on Disney+ for the first time alongside YouTube and Twitch.

title: Trump Frustrated With Vance Over Iran War Criticism as Rubio Gains Favour
summary: Donald Trump has grown increasingly frustrated with Vice President JD Vance over his criticism of the Iran war, The New York Times reported, while privately praising Secretary of State Marco Rubio as a possible presidential contender in 2028.
imageCredit: President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance — Photo: The White House, Wikimedia Commons (public domain)
imageNote: Free-licence White House photo of President Donald Trump with Vice President JD Vance. The photo also shows Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.
body: US President Donald Trump has grown increasingly frustrated with Vice President JD Vance over his criticism of the war against Iran, The New York Times reported on Wednesday. According to people familiar with the president’s private conversations, Trump has complained to aides and allies that Vance should have said the decision to launch the war was the right one, even while acknowledging its political cost.

The tension follows Vance’s lengthy social media post after the November 3 midterm elections, in which he blamed the Iran war for the Republican Party’s losses. “The reason we lost is the war,” Vance wrote, adding that losing the Senate for the next six years was the price paid. Democrats won control of both chambers of Congress in the elections. Trump initially appeared to agree with much of Vance’s assessment, telling reporters, “I think it’s largely true.”

In the two weeks since, however, Trump has privately vented that Vance failed to defend the decision itself. Trump told reporters over the weekend that Vance should also have said the strikes were necessary, describing the campaign as one of the best things the administration has done because Iran must not be allowed to obtain a nuclear weapon. Trump has also told Vance to shift his attention away from negotiations with Iran.

At the same time, Trump has been complimentary in private about Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who has repeatedly defended the war as essential to American national security, and has suggested Rubio could be a strong presidential contender in 2028. Vance, who is also seen as a possible 2028 candidate, denied any rift in a Fox News interview on Monday, insisting there is “no daylight” between him and the president. The White House did not respond to a request for comment, and Vance’s office declined to comment.

title: Ashton Kutcher's $435 Million Anthropic Bet Pays Off as Record IPO Briefly Tops $2 Trillion
summary: Anthropic's record stock market debut turned Ashton Kutcher's venture firm Sound Ventures' early $435 million bet into a stake worth about $7 billion, as the AI company behind Claude briefly topped a $2 trillion market value on its first day of trading.
imageCredit: Ashton Kutcher on stage in 2022 — Photo: Isame90, Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 4.0)
imageNote: Free-licence photo of Ashton Kutcher speaking on stage. No free-licence photo of Kutcher with the Anthropic team exists.
body: Anthropic, the artificial intelligence company behind the Claude chatbot, made a record-breaking stock market debut on Thursday, November 19, after pricing its shares at $83 each the night before. The offering valued the company at about $1.5 trillion, and shares opened at $111.50 on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT, briefly pushing its market value above $2 trillion on the first day of trading. The IPO raised $81.3 billion, making Anthropic the first frontier AI lab to go public.

Among the biggest winners is Sound Ventures, the venture capital firm co-founded by actor Ashton Kutcher and talent manager Guy Oseary. The firm invested $35 million in Anthropic's 2023 funding round, when the company was valued at around $5 billion, and went on to invest about $400 million more, bringing its total to roughly $435 million, according to Bloomberg. Sound Ventures now owns about 0.5 percent of Anthropic, a stake worth about $7 billion at the IPO price.

Kutcher publicly congratulated Anthropic chief executive Dario Amodei and his team on the debut, reflecting that the outcome was the result of years of building conviction in the company and the technology rather than a single investment. Kutcher stepped down as a Sound Ventures partner in July and remains a senior adviser, while Oseary continues to run the firm alongside managing partner Effie Epstein.

The $7 billion figure is the value of the firm's stake, not Kutcher's personal fortune: Sound Ventures manages capital for outside investors, so any eventual proceeds would be shared among them. Even so, the debut turns one of Hollywood's most closely watched venture bets into a roughly sixteenfold paper gain, and it caps a week in which Anthropic's listing became the largest IPO in stock market history.

title: Hunger Games Stars Reunite as 'Sunrise on the Reaping' Opens in Theatres
summary: Jennifer Lawrence, Josh Hutcherson and Woody Harrelson reunited on the New York red carpet this week as The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping opens in theatres, returning the franchise to a young Haymitch's 50th Games.
imageCredit: Jennifer Lawrence at the 83rd Academy Awards — Photo: Mingle MediaTV, Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 2.0)
imageNote: Free-licence photo of Jennifer Lawrence, who returned for a cameo in Sunrise on the Reaping. No free-licence photo of the 2026 premiere exists.
body: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping opens in theatres on Friday, November 20, and the film's New York world premiere earlier this week brought the franchise's original stars back together. Jennifer Lawrence and Josh Hutcherson reunited on the red carpet at Alice Tully Hall on Monday, November 16, joined by former co-stars Woody Harrelson, Elizabeth Banks, Jena Malone and Amandla Stenberg, fourteen years after the original film premiered in March 2012.

The new film is set 24 years before the first Hunger Games and follows a 16-year-old Haymitch Abernathy, played by Joseph Zada, as he is chosen as a tribute from District 12 for the 50th Hunger Games, the Second Quarter Quell, which enlists double the usual number of tributes. Harrelson, who played Haymitch in all four original films, returns for a cameo, as do Lawrence and Hutcherson as Katniss Everdeen and Peeta Mellark.

Directed by Francis Lawrence from a screenplay by Billy Ray and Michael Lesslie, and based on Suzanne Collins' best-selling novel, the prequel also stars Ralph Fiennes as President Snow, Elle Fanning as a young Effie Trinket, Jesse Plemons, Glenn Close, Kieran Culkin, Maya Hawke, Whitney Peak, Kelvin Harrison Jr., Ben Wang and Mckenna Grace. Tom Blyth and Rachel Zegler, who starred in the 2023 prequel The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes, also walked the red carpet in support of the new cast.

The premiere capped a week of early screenings and fan events ahead of the film's theatrical release, with the original cast's reunion drawing the loudest cheers of the night. Sunrise on the Reaping is in theatres only from November 20, 2026.

title: Hackers Breach US Agriculture Department System That Sends Payments to Farmers
summary: Hackers breached a US Department of Agriculture system used to send payments to farmers, NBC News reported on Friday, as the department reset passwords and worked to restore loan and payment tools knocked offline all week.
imageCredit: The USDA headquarters area in Washington, D.C. — Photo: USDA, Wikimedia Commons (public domain)
imageNote: File photo of the USDA headquarters area in Washington, D.C. No free-licence photo of the 2026 incident exists.
body: Hackers this week breached a system the US Department of Agriculture uses to send payments to farmers, NBC News reported on Friday, November 20, citing two former USDA officials with knowledge of the matter. The department notified employees of the incident on Thursday, the officials said.

The breach surfaced during a week of outages at the department. An internal email sent on Monday, November 16, said the USDA's Cybersecurity and Privacy Operations Center had uncovered a security incident and that all database passwords had to be reset in every environment, knocking farmer-facing tools offline. Employees reported outages in the Farm Service Agency's loan software, the Natural Resources Conservation Service's ProTracts payment program and its Service Desk mapping software.

Richard Fordyce, the USDA's undersecretary for farm production and conservation, confirmed the cyberthreat to reporters and said no personal information was exposed and no data was lost. He said most systems should be back online by the close of business on Friday, with work continuing over the weekend if needed. Farm Service Agency administrator Bill Beam also confirmed the outages.

The payments database is the known extent of the intrusion so far, but the former officials warned that the compromised system could provide a backdoor to more sensitive information, including food safety data and research on animal-borne illnesses. It is not known who was responsible, and the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency referred questions to the USDA. Intelligence officials told Congress on Wednesday that a series of recent technology outages at government agencies were separate incidents, not evidence of a coordinated cyberattack.

title: Melania Trump's New Docuseries Gets Zero Stars as Critics Call It 'Entirely Skippable'
summary: Melania: The Series, the two-part Prime Video follow-up to the first lady's January documentary, premiered on November 20 to harsh reviews, with USA Today giving it zero stars out of four.
imageCredit: Melania Trump's official White House portrait, 2025 — Photo: White House, Wikimedia Commons (public domain)
imageNote: Official 2025 White House portrait. No free-licence photo of the series itself was available.
body: Melania: The Series, a two-part follow-up to first lady Melania Trump's January documentary, premiered on Amazon's Prime Video on Friday, November 20, 2026, following a premiere the previous evening at New York's Lincoln Center. The series, directed by Brett Ratner, revisits the 20 days leading up to President Donald Trump's second inauguration in 2025, drawing largely on footage left over from the earlier film.

Critics have been unsparing. USA Today gave the series zero stars out of four, calling it "entirely skippable" and saying there is "nothing new" in it. The Guardian described it as "a dead-eyed advert that barely manages to masquerade as entertainment", while The Telegraph awarded two stars out of five and called it "glossy propaganda". Reviewers agreed the two episodes, neither of which reaches 40 minutes, reveal little about their subject.

The series' two episodes are titled "Family & Trust" and "Pride & Honor". Melania Trump speaks for much of both instalments, discussing her life as a wife, mother and first lady, including meeting Donald Trump in New York in 1998 and their marriage in Florida in 2005. The second episode follows her visits to victims of Hurricane Helene in North Carolina and the California wildfires, before turning to her work with foster children.

The poor reception follows a similar split for the original film. Amazon spent a reported $75 million to make and market the January documentary, which holds a 9% critics' score on Rotten Tomatoes against a 99% verified audience score. At Thursday's premiere, the first lady described the series as an opportunity for audiences to better understand her beliefs, principles, family and personal values.

title: Sam Kinison's Estate Signs With Buchwald for AI Avatar of Late Comedian
summary: The late comedian's estate has signed with the Buchwald talent agency to develop an AI avatar of Sam Kinison, built by the Uare.AI platform, more than 30 years after his death in 1992.
imageCredit: Sam Kinison (centre) at The Comedy Store, c. 1980s — Photo: The World Famous Comedy Store, Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 2.0)
imageNote: Free-licence photo of Kinison at The Comedy Store in the 1980s, with Carl LaBove. No free-licence image of the AI avatar itself exists.
body: The estate of late comedian Sam Kinison has signed with the Buchwald talent agency to develop new business opportunities around his name and likeness, including an AI avatar, Variety reported on Friday, November 20, 2026. The avatar is powered by Uare.AI, the artificial intelligence platform founded by LivePerson founder Rob LoCascio. The estate is managed by Kinison's brother and former manager, Bill Kinison.

Buchwald says the avatar could "expand opportunities" for Kinison "across multiple verticals". Among the possible uses are streaming comedy specials featuring new AI-generated performances, brand partnerships and commercial appearances, documentary and biographical content, potential hologram concert tours or live venue appearances, and licensing for film, television and digital media projects.

"Sam was always on the cutting edge of comedy and entertainment, and with the genius of Uare.AI's work and the Buchwald agency's vision, we're keeping the promise of my brother's legacy alive," Bill Kinison said in a statement. "I can't wait to see what Sam will do!"

Kinison, who died in a car accident on April 10, 1992, at the age of 38, became one of the defining stand-up comics of the 1980s with his screaming, high-energy delivery, honed during his years as a Pentecostal preacher before he turned to comedy. His breakout came on HBO's Rodney Dangerfield's Ninth Annual Young Comedians Special in 1985. The deal comes as other estates explore similar arrangements: the Stan Lee and Judy Garland estates are sorting out deals with the AI company ElevenLabs, which has also signed Sir Michael Caine to use an AI-rendered imitation of his voice. No specific projects or dates for the Kinison avatar have been announced.

title: Verstappen Wins Wild Las Vegas Grand Prix After 35 Lead Changes
summary: Max Verstappen held off Lando Norris by 0.639 seconds to win a breathless Las Vegas Grand Prix on Saturday night, his third victory on the Strip in four years, in a race that featured 35 lead changes and 352 overtakes.
imageCredit: Max Verstappen at the 2025 Italian Grand Prix — Photo: Eustace Bagge, Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 4.0)
imageNote: Free-licence photo of Verstappen in his Red Bull at Monza in 2025. No free-licence photo of the 2026 Las Vegas race itself exists yet.
body: Max Verstappen won the Las Vegas Grand Prix on Saturday night, November 21, 2026, holding off a race-long challenge to take his third victory on the streets of Nevada in four years. The Red Bull driver beat McLaren's Lando Norris by 0.639 seconds, with Oscar Piastri third, in a 50-lap race that featured 35 lead changes and 352 overtakes.

Verstappen started from pole position but could never break away, as the slipstream down the Las Vegas Strip kept the field nose-to-tail under the floodlights. George Russell repeatedly passed him for the lead, as did his Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli, but Verstappen kept enough energy in reserve to sweep back past at Turn 17 each time. "That was crazy. Really, really surreal and something I've never seen before in Formula One myself," Verstappen said afterwards.

The decisive drama came in the closing laps. Russell, who had started on the front row, ran into the barriers with three laps remaining and finished ninth. Antonelli, the 20-year-old who became the youngest ever Formula One world champion earlier this month, then slowed suddenly on the penultimate lap, letting both McLarens through. Norris and Piastri had spent their remaining battery fighting each other, and with no energy left to attack the leader, Verstappen took the chequered flag with the top five covered by just three seconds.

It was Verstappen's fourth win in six races and the 75th of his Formula One career, and it moved him 37 points clear of Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton in second place in the drivers' standings, with two races of the season remaining. Mercedes have already wrapped up both championships. Hamilton and Ferrari team-mate Charles Leclerc collided during the race, both collecting 10-second penalties, and finished seventh and tenth.

title: Australian Music Icon Molly Meldrum Dies Aged 83
summary: Ian 'Molly' Meldrum, the Countdown host who championed Australian music for six decades, has died in Melbourne aged 83 after a long illness, his family has announced.
imageCredit: Meldrum at the ARIA Awards in 2009 — Photo: Jeanie Mackinder, Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 2.0)
imageNote: Free-licence photo of Meldrum in his trademark Stetson at the 2009 ARIA Awards. No free-licence photo from 2026 exists.
body: Ian “Molly” Meldrum, the Australian television presenter and music producer who spent six decades championing homegrown music, has died aged 83. His family said in a statement that he died at Epworth Hospital in Richmond, Melbourne, early on Monday, 23 November 2026, after a long illness. No cause of death was given.

Meldrum is best known for his 13-year stint hosting Countdown, the ABC music programme he helped create in 1974. The show turned acts such as Skyhooks and Sherbet into national names, and Meldrum used it to champion local artists alongside international stars from INXS to ABBA, interviewing figures including Elton John and Britain’s King Charles along the way. He was inducted into the ARIA Hall of Fame, and in 1969 he had produced his first number one record, Russell Morris’s “The Real Thing”.

Born in Orbost, Victoria, on 29 January 1943, Meldrum began his career as a music journalist in London and worked as a publicist for the Beatles’ Apple Records before returning to Australia. He remained a fixture of Australian music life for decades, and was seriously injured after falling from a ladder at his home in 2011, drawing well-wishes from artists including Boy George and Kylie Minogue.

Tributes poured in from across Australia on Monday. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese said in a post on X that “an enthusiasm that was uncontainable, Molly Meldrum loved music almost as much as we loved him”. Meldrum is survived by his long-term partner, Yan Wongngam, and his adopted son, Morgan Scholes.

title: Joe Russo Confirms Avengers: Doomsday Will Run About Two and a Half Hours
summary: Co-director Joe Russo has confirmed that Marvel's Avengers: Doomsday will run about two and a half hours when it opens in cinemas on December 18, 2026 — close to Infinity War's length and around half an hour shorter than Endgame.
imageCredit: Joe Russo and Tom Hiddleston at San Diego Comic-Con in 2017 — Photo: Gage Skidmore, Wikimedia Commons (CC BY-SA 2.0)
imageNote: Free-licence photo of Russo with Tom Hiddleston at the 2017 San Diego Comic-Con, for Avengers: Infinity War. No free-licence image of Doomsday itself exists.
body: Avengers: Doomsday will run about two and a half hours, co-director Joe Russo has confirmed. Speaking at the Qatar Film Committee's second Doha Industry Days, Russo said the character teasers and clips Marvel has been releasing are “all pieces of something that are going to equal two and a half hours of your time on December 18,” according to Deadline. The film opens in cinemas on December 18, 2026.

At around 150 minutes, Doomsday would sit close to Avengers: Infinity War, which ran two hours and 29 minutes, and well short of Avengers: Endgame at three hours and one minute. Earlier reports had pointed to a longer cut: The Hollywood Reporter reported a runtime of 165 minutes, or two hours and 45 minutes, when premium-format ticket sales began on July 20, 2026, while Brazilian outlet Omelete reported two hours, 29 minutes and 36 seconds for standard screenings. Russo's wording is approximate, so the final cut could still shift slightly, and his brother Anthony Russo told Fandango the film is “a two-and-a-half-hour movie, or so.”

Joe and Anthony Russo return to direct their first Marvel film in seven years, with former Iron Man star Robert Downey Jr. taking on a new role as the villain Doctor Doom. The film brings together the Avengers, the Fantastic Four and the X-Men against Doom, and it opens on the same day as Dune: Part Three. It arrives a day earlier in India, on December 17.

Fans are also watching for a new teaser or trailer, with expectations that one could arrive on Monday, November 23. Russo told fans to keep refreshing their feeds, hinting that a final trailer could still land before the film's release.
